title:
Disk Forensics
Process Flows
subtitle: Acquisition → artifact creation → grounded reports

pages.title: Disk / Evidence-to-report overview
pages.intro: Every result traces back to an immutable acquisition or a clearly identified derivative. Extraction, artifact creation, RAG and reporting have separate completion gates.

nodes.text:
Case + image / folder
Intake and source plan

Review source media
Create evidence descriptions

Wait / fail / coverage gap
Preserve checkpoints

notes: Resource policy
One active serial stage per job; up to four CPU evidence workers inside a stage. OCR and vision share a single GPU permit. Embeddings are not a stage.
Evidence policy
Do not infer deleted status, content, identity or suspicious intent from a filename. Record a source locator, hash, evidence state and the reason for each observation.

pages.title: The 13 controlled stages
pages.intro: The same serial controller governs Disk evidence after acquisition handoff. One stage owns the job at a time; bounded workers may operate inside a stage.
notes: State meanings

Ready means the configured gates completed. coverage_complete and exception counters still describe missing or inaccessible evidence. A completed acquisition does not prove that every possible artifact was captured.

pages.intro: Choose the accessible source folder before processing. Intake links the job to its case and records the intended examination.

notes: Fail early
Incomplete image segments, an unreadable selected directory or an inaccessible drive must be visible before a parser job is dispatched.
Resume
Keep the source plan and progress checkpoint. A previously finalized acquisition can hand off to artifacts without repeating the image walk.

pages.title: 02 / Read-only source preparation
pages.intro: The preparation step exposes acquired source bytes to extraction. It does not alter the original evidence image.

nodes.text:

Segment / path metadata

or prepared source path

notes: Source integrity
Keep original segment/path identifiers. Partitions and filesystem entries remain linked to their source image.
Support boundary
The flow records the filesystems and bytes the implemented readers expose. An unsupported encrypted volume requires an authorized decrypted source; preparation is not universal volume decryption.

pages.title: 03 / Extraction, storage and finalization
pages.intro: Extraction walks readable roots, stores acquired bytes and records a finalized index. File-level failures remain explicit.

nodes.text:

remaining source files

Path + reason + count

notes: Finalize barrier
The manifest is the durable handoff. Acquisition milestones are recorded at finalization; later evidence stages do not silently rewrite the original image.
Performance
Use resumable extraction plans, sharded indexes and bounded file workers. Counts include failed and skipped paths so a fast partial acquisition cannot masquerade as complete coverage.

pages.title: 04 / Manifest-to-artifact materialization
pages.intro: Each acquired file receives a stable artifact identity before parsing or model review.

nodes.text:
Create job_artifacts
Path, size, MIME, SHA-256

Object / part locator
Source metadata + state

notes: Provenance
An artifact can be an acquired file or an identified derivative. Its path, content hash, storage locator and evidence state must distinguish those cases.
Bounded work
Paging and stable identities support large acquisitions without duplicate artifact rows after a retry.

pages.title: 05 / Native parsing and format dispatch
pages.intro: Identify content from signatures and structure as well as extensions. Binary candidates stay labeled when their schema or meaning is unverified.

nodes.text:
Inspect signature, MIME
and parser registry

Encrypted / unknown binary

Native structured parse
Documents / mail / DBs

Text + normalized rows
Table / row / source hashes

notes: Supported families
EML, EMLX, MSG, MBOX/MBX and attachments; office/PDF/text documents; JSON/JSONL/NDJSON, XML, CSV/TSV, plist/bplist and supported SQLite tables.
Quality
Native database rows are stronger than unverified binary or protobuf fragments. A filename or printable string is not enough to call a file a conversation database.

pages.title: Priority / Web, email and WhatsApp-linked media
pages.intro: Priority records preserve the distinction between actual browser events, copied URLs and attachment references.

notes: Web coverage
Collect acquired history, bookmarks, download records, cookies and login metadata. Protected credentials and encrypted web stores are inventoried unless a supported decryption route is available.
WhatsApp

Disk-resident WhatsApp databases/backups use available matching keys and the same authenticated parser path documented in the Mobile PDF. A WhatsApp web URL does not prove decrypted chats were recovered.

pages.title: 06 / Recovery and deleted-data evidence states
pages.intro: Recovery examines acquired retained bytes. It cannot reconstruct overwritten or unavailable content merely from metadata.

nodes.text:
Acquired DB / filesystem
Retained bytes + metadata

Recycle / retained files
SQLite residual scan

Deleted / retained evidence
Marker + byte provenance

Recovered or candidate
Separate evidence state

notes: Interpretation
A row found in an old backup is historical evidence, not automatic proof that a user deleted the current chat. Residual candidates need corroboration.
Limits
This flow does not promise recovery of all unallocated image sectors or encrypted/overwritten deleted files. The source reader and retained bytes determine actual coverage.

pages.title: 07 / OCR and searchable text
pages.intro: OCR processes acquired pixels and document pages. It records success, empty results and failures separately.

notes: Scheduling
OCR and vision share one GPU permit. A legitimate permit or model wait is visible to progressAgent and is not classified as an invalid halt.
Evidence
OCR is derived text. Keep the original file, page/frame reference, source hash and OCR status; an OCR guess does not replace the original evidence.

pages.title: 08 / Image and video evidence review
pages.intro: Suspicious Activity is created from observable source content and its provenance. Filenames alone do not establish suspicious conduct.

nodes.text:
Sample every 10 s
plus final sample

notes: Exact evidence
Retain artifact ID, original path/hash, model and description. Video evidence also retains decoded presentation time, derived frame PNG and frame hash.
Scope

Images are resized for review up to 1536 px; animated images use the first frame. Video sampling is not an examination of every frame. Missing models or decode failures produce a wait or recorded gap; model interpretation needs examiner review.

pages.title: 09 / Normalize, correlate and classify artifacts
pages.intro: Durable source files, native records and derivatives join the inventory without losing their different evidence strengths.

nodes.text:
Join source artifact
DB row + attachment links

Regular artifact category
Retain source state

notes: One evidence category
Suspicious Activity includes supported chat/mail text, web/download/file/application indicators, OCR and actual image/video observations. Each entry carries a source-backed explanation.
Review
Suspicious is a review flag, not a finding of guilt. Unverified fragments and inferred links remain identified as such.

pages.title: 10 / Text-only RAG chunking
pages.intro: The embedding stage and forensic vector search are removed. The RAG source is normalized text, parsed content, OCR and evidence descriptions.

nodes.text:
Replace stale policy
Write chunk records

notes: Window definition
The limit is characters, not tokens. Headers count inside the 2500-character window. Maximum nominal advance is 1700 characters; boundaries can adjust to the content.
Query / report
Retrieval uses text search and evidence references. No GPU embeddings or CLIP retrieval are required. Indexing source descriptions does not add facts beyond the cited source content.

pages.title: 11–12 / Entities and evidence graph
pages.intro: Enrichment runs after durable chunks. Graph writes preserve source relationships and use idempotent keys.

nodes.text:
Extract identities, URLs
Times and identifiers

notes: Identity
A chat account, sender, image path or URL links to the actual acquired record. Matching names or filenames remain weaker correlation signals.
Dependency gate
A graph dependency wait holds the serial gate. progressAgent checks the wait reason and retries within policy; it must not report the job ready while the required stage remains waiting.

pages.title: 13 / Validation and readiness
pages.intro: Validation compares required stage outputs and checkpoints. Coverage status is retained alongside readiness.

notes: Readiness vs completeness
Ready means this acquisition finished its configured stages. An unsupported encrypted source, missing bytes or recorded decode failure remains an explicit coverage limitation.
Retry
Resume only incomplete derived stages and preserve acquired bytes. Report regeneration uses new derived records rather than retroactively changing a saved report.

pages.title: The single progressAgent supervisor
pages.intro: progressAgent is the sole outside-process coordinator. Observe, Performance and Repair huddles are retired; queued legacy huddles perform no work.

nodes.text:
Keep owned process
Expose reason / deadline

Inspect owned task
Lease and deadline

Cancel owned subprocess
Clean matched lease

notes: Valid waits
User pause, a shared GPU permit, a required model/dependency, or an operation inside its expected deadline may legitimately exceed one minute. A fresh heartbeat alone is not useful progress.
Ownership / cleanup
Recovery stops only the owned job process and matched leases. Routine legacy huddle lines are hidden from consoles; historical database rows and processing/evidence logs remain intact.

pages.title: Report / Intake, scope and evidence selection
pages.intro: A report run starts from saved case intake and selected evidence. Disk uses image/source details and the finalized extraction.

nodes.text:

Expose gap; do not draft

Create report run
Single run owner

Clear stale caches

notes: Refresh scope
Refresh reads the existing acquisition. Report generation does not acquire a missing phone database or remount an unavailable original source to invent evidence.
Selection
Retain selected artifact counts, objectives, procedure and examiner observations. Saved historic reports keep their content; a new run is needed to include new derived evidence.

pages.title: Report / Grounded section generation
pages.intro: Sections share a deterministic order. Structured facts and saved observations are preferred where the report has direct evidence.

nodes.text:
Render saved facts
Artifact / profile references

Flag / correct section
Factual fallback if needed

Final report content
Ready for review / export

notes: Model boundary
The model can describe source facts. Unsupported claims, incomplete evidence and failed generation are reported explicitly; factual templates provide fallback content.
Resuming
Section checkpoints and a single report owner support pause/resume. progressAgent tracks actual work, section state and valid model/dependency waits.

pages.title: Report / Suspicious Activity evidence panels
pages.intro: The report draws this section from source-linked artifacts and verified media, then allows examiner observations to be added.

notes: Text evidence
Chats, email, browsing, downloads and application indicators cite their native record locator and explanation. A URL reference alone does not establish browsing or downloading.
Media evidence
Present the actual retained image or sampled video frame with its description. Frame timestamps locate evidence in the video; a sampled frame does not represent the complete video.

pages.title: Report / Common section and page structure
pages.intro: The shared renderer keeps the Disk and Mobile report sections aligned. Platform-specific source headings are substituted without changing the surrounding structure.
notes: Shared formatting
A4 page width, section spacing, header, watermark, page numbers, evidence captions and annexure links use the same rendering path.
Content and pagination
Fourteen logical sections are saved in the report run. Evidence volume determines the page count; identical layout does not imply identical length.
Suspicious Activity
This is a dedicated report section and artifact category. It includes source-linked reasons, real retained media or sampled frames, and separate examiner observations.

pages.title: Report / Shared layout, review and export
pages.intro: Disk reports use the shared report renderer and section order. The number of pages changes with the evidence; page styling and alignment are shared.

nodes.text:
Saved section content
Review grades + citations

Shared A4 page renderer
Headers + watermark

notes: Media alignment
Use verified source pictures and derived video frame images with captions, artifact IDs, paths/hashes and frame timestamps. Keep examiner observations distinct from model descriptions.
Limits
The shared layout does not force Disk and Mobile reports to have identical page counts. Missing source pixels or unverified deleted-data candidates must not be presented as exact recovered media.

pages.title: Verification, performance and implementation map
pages.intro: Source tracing describes what the package does. Live hardware acceptance is a separate result.
notes: Performance already in code

Bounded workers, manifest paging/checkpoints, source-preserving resume, text-only RAG and serialized GPU inference reduce contention. A waiting model or large file is evaluated against its stage deadline.
Deployment
Use the existing Disk/Mobile serial deployment instructions in DISK-MOBILE-SERIAL-RELEASE.md. The scanner update scripts affect the vulnerability services, not the source evidence acquisition.
